### 2026-10-18 – Hellos, this is going to be a LOOONG entry bc i just finished a long grind filled with sketches, discovering new functions and shouting at the computer because it just doesnt work lol. Baaaasically as

**6h**

Hellos, this is going to be a LOOONG entry bc i just finished a long grind filled with sketches, discovering new functions and shouting at the computer because it just doesnt work lol. Baaaasically as i said in my idea reel i want to make a marble run where the marbles are not only collected automatically, so you only turn a lever or idk hook a motor up and that has a little metal sheet (aluminum maybe???) to make beautiful sound.

The thing is, i have NO experience with cad (with onshape at least) so i had to learn everything while missing some features that civil 3d has. I started making the collector part (IDK how to call it)

Basically it is a half sphrere that catches the marble and takes it to the top to throw it back ac=gain in the system, i was thinking of making idk like not using this part but i figured ill try to make it and then ill see if i change the system later on, however i do think i did better than i expected. The first foto u se is the part that carries the ball, youll see it is hanging on for dear life at the edge, i didnt know any better and it was the first part i ever did. Funnily enough i did a sphere and the subtracted a rectangle prism(?)  and another sphere to achieve that form and then scraped it and did it using the more simple way revolve.

Then youll see the tracks for the revolving thingy, im still tweaking it but i am quite proud that i managed to do it. While using transform seems like the more reasonable way to do it. I DID NOT KNOW any better oke? I re did the sketch on different planes to the extrude each one in order to achieve that form. I am planning on adding in some ridges in the middle to guide the track but thats something ill figure out tomorrow considering i must finish the whole thing tomorrow.

Then we have the cone, that wasnt THAT hard actually, considering i had already drawn on multiple planes, what was somewhat hard was turning the whole thing, bc i kept having to find the idk axis thingy, i dodnt remember the name, but the thing that defined along which axis it turns and it kept doing CRAZY things.  The cone has a simple slit and hole for the collector and the tracks, but i am planing on chanign it in the future for it to fit more accurately.

### 2026-10-18 – OMGGGGGG IM DONEEEEEEEEE

**7h**

OMGGGGGG IM DONEEEEEEEEE

Guys using onshape as a kinda absolute beginner was TOUGH, not necessarily bc it was that hard but i had some experience with other software and i REALLY MISSED some functions like array polar and more comprehensive rotate transform but overall i think i succeeded. Today i grinded to finish the whole thing.

I started with fixing the railing of the project, i had previously made a railing for the project but if didnt have and ridges for the chain component to stay in place, so i redesigned it and left space for the teeth that slide with the gear of the lever. That also meant i had to enhance my previous design of the chain component to have not only teeth but also a locking mechanism (OFC i cared about clearance what u thought). It was quite hard, however, to see the dimensions of the ridges to make sure the teeth fit and also the locking mechanism, but i made it. Another problem i stumbled upon with the collection system is that i planned to use the same dish that collects the balls to drop them, but AHA that wouldnt work bc the balls would fall straight through, so i make another one and put it next to the curve of the system so the chain component acts as kind of a catapult and the balls fall not through the opening for the chain component but rather through the hole in the middle.

Then i went on to make the base, as i needed the collection mechanism to fit i needed to leave a hole for the bottom loop of the railing and leave enough CLEAREANCE for the chain. The supports are simple columns and i used the subtract tool to make them, i made the tool copy of the parts it is meant to hold SLIGHTLY larger to make up for the glue so that t is a tight fit.

One of the hardest parts (in the sense that i had explained earlier) is that i needed to make a gear without array polar, but since the chain always has teeth i ended up using a polygon instead, i had to check that when spinning the leaver, at least one pin touched the chain and i think it does.

Then there is the support for the leaver, OFC i cared about clearence and there isnt much to that, i used the subtract tool with a slightly larger leaver model. OH RIGHT, the tracks, MY GAWD they were hard, onshape was FREAKING out bc my like track face wasnt EXACTLY on the begining of the path, but i just moved the plane and it worked so there is that.

FINALLY, this was acc the first part i did in this session but i left is at the end bc it is the heart of my build. THE MARBLEPHONE. It is a 5mm thick aluminum plate that when hit makes notes of the fourth octave. IT NEEDS to sit slightly above the chaisis it is in for it to make a sound but besides that is is quite a nice adition. Here are the measurements i used.
